findings.where: Whole tile: the first screen and every specimen below it
findings.fault: Mark is never shown. The tile has no portrait and no slot or treatment for one, so the only figure on the sheet is a drawing of the logo's arches. Client value 3 ('the man himself: Mark is seen') goes unanswered, and so does first-visit trust item 1 (a named, real person with a photo of his face).
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer looking at a solo advisor wants to see the person they would hire. Mark asked to be seen and heard, and the brief says every tile answers each client value.

findings.where: Article specimen, and every post Angélique adds
findings.fault: The look has no answer for a photograph. Nothing shows how a photo from a LinkedIn post or an article image would sit on the diazo sheet, so the first post with a picture will be placed by guesswork against a ground built for white linework.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who must add posts and PDFs without a designer (value 9). Mark too, who wants the images refreshed (§6).

findings.where: Article specimen: the body text, pull quote and PDF link
findings.fault: The long-form reading surface is the same gridded blueprint ground as the hero. A whole article is light text on saturated blue, with the 20 mm grid lines running through the lines of prose. The palette has no calmer reading surface for the article pages, which are the site's Read mode.
findings.who_objects: A reader working through one of Mark's PPP articles. Over several screens, reversed text over a ruled pattern tires the eye and pulls attention from the argument.

findings.where: Nav bar logo (and, by extension, the hero drawing of the mark)
findings.fault: The logo is shown in a reversed, all-white version: white arches and a white MMM INFRA wordmark instead of the logo's blue #0070C0 and grey #404040. The client holds no white version and has not approved one. The palette also never names the logo's blue or grey, either as tokens or as logo-only colours.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo 'stays' (value 7). The brand rules allow a version the client doesn't hold only with his yes. The logo blue next to diazo blue is also left unresolved for the layout round.

findings.where: Hero, the identity lines under MARK M. MOSELEY, and the circled 'A' marker
findings.fault: The role line 'Infrastructure advisor' is set in the same style as the drawing caption 'Longitudinal section A-A · Scale NTS'. They read as one label, and the visitor's one plain statement of what Mark does sits in the same type as drafting jargon. 'NTS' also appears three times on the first screen, and the circled 'A' beside the name reads as an avatar or control rather than a section mark.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor taking the 5-second test, who has to read past engineering notation to find who this is and what he does. Mark too, whose role is weakened by the conceit.

findings.where: Hero drawing, the amber hatch in the third bay; palette, Sodium Amber
findings.fault: The amber is the one action's colour (the Write to Mark button), but it also fills a decorative hatch in the drawing. That hatch is the brightest thing on the first screen and pulls the eye away from the button. The palette gives one colour two jobs: 'daylight in the drawing, and the one action'.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to get in touch. The action's colour should mean 'act here' and nothing else, and here it first lands on a static drawing.

findings.where: Nav bar title block: the DRAWING MMM-GA-001 and SCALE NTS cells
findings.fault: Two static cells sit in the nav row, boxed exactly like the nav links and in the same light colour, so they look like more destinations. On phone they take the top row beside the logo and push the real navigation onto a second row.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who taps 'MMM-GA-001' expecting a page and gets nothing. Phone visitors also lose header room to decoration.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the REPLAY THE CUT button
findings.fault: A button that acts in place is styled as an underlined text link. The underline is the link's reserved signifier, so the control borrows the look of navigation.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects an underlined phrase to take them somewhere. A small mismatch in a specimen the layout round will copy.

findings.where: Article specimen: the title and the byline date
findings.fault: The specimen breaks the type pair's own rules. The type pair says headings are ExtraBold capitals, but the article title is in mixed case. It says dates are mono only, but the byline date '18 September 2024' is in the sans, while the PDF row's date '2026-04-23' is in mono and in another format.
findings.who_objects: The layout round and Angélique, who will copy whichever of the two contradictory examples they see first, so headings and dates drift across the site.

findings.where: Hero drawing, right end of the ground line
findings.fault: A lone thin curve rises from the ground line past the end of the band and stops in mid-air at the frame. It has no label and no counterpart, so it reads as a stray stroke rather than part of the section.
findings.who_objects: An engineer or lawyer used to drawings, for whom an unexplained line on a general arrangement looks like an error on the first thing they see.

findings.fault: The box loses its inner padding. The Earth Hatch swatch and its label sit hard against the box's left edge, the Poche swatch runs to the right edge, and an empty band holds the dimension bar. The desktop version is evenly inset.
findings.who_objects: Anyone reviewing the tile on a phone, who sees the texture specimen looking broken next to the evenly inset palette above it.
